subject: DPA: Subprocessor disclosure & EU data transfers (FinServCo procurement)
messages:
From: Ellen Dobson <ellen.dobson@finservco.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finservco.com, legal@finservco.com
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA and subprocessor details needed to close purchase order

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement needs a fully executed DPA and an up-to-date subprocessor list before we can push the PO through. Our legal team spotted three items in your DPA redline that require clarification:

- Cross-border transfer mechanism: we see Standard Contractual Clauses referenced but need confirmation you rely only on SCCs (no SCC + additional approvals) and whether onward transfers to any non-EEA subprocessors occur.
- Subprocessor notice window: our security policy requires 30 days prior notice for onboarding subprocessors that process EU personal data.
- Data retention & deletion: we have a strict 90-day minimum deletion period for cached data unless otherwise agreed.

I attached the DPA you provided and our procurement checklist. Can you confirm next steps and whether you can accept the attached redlines, or propose a DocuSign envelope for signature? We are targeting contract execution by 2026-03-22 to align with our quarter close.

Best,
Ellen
Ellen Dobson
Senior Procurement Manager
FinServCo
[Attachment: DPA_FinServCo_redline_v1.docx] [Attachment: Subprocessor_Disclosure_20260314.xlsx]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Ellen Dobson <ellen.dobson@finservco.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA and subprocessor details needed to close purchase order

Hi Ellen — appreciate the clear checklist and timeline. Quick answers up front:

- Cross-border transfers: Redwood relies on the EU SCCs for EEA -> US transfers; we also maintain an internal transfer risk assessment and will not perform onward transfers to subprocessors outside the locations documented in our subprocessor workbook without prior notice.
- Subprocessor notice window: our standard is 14 days; we can discuss a one-time exception for your account to extend to 30 days for EU data.
- Data retention: our product allows configurable cache TTLs. We can commit to a 90-day deletion policy for any cached personal data tied to your tenant; engineering will confirm how to operationalize this in Dedicated and Hosted modes.

I'm looping in Monica from Legal to coordinate formal redlines and get the DPA routed for signature. Given your 3/22 target, we'll prioritize this — Monica, can you review the attached redline and advise if we can accept the 30-day notice or if we need an exception?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DataFlowDiagram.pdf]

From: monica_patel@redwood.com

Date: 2026-03-15T12:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA and subprocessor details needed to close purchase order

FYI — forwarding FinServCo's checklist and redline. High level: their requests are reasonable but the 30-day prior notice for subprocessor onboarding is materially different from our standard 14-day notice and has operational impact. Also need a technical answer on "onward transfers" language in section 4.

I've marked up DPA_FinServCo_redline_v1.docx and propose two paths:
1) Accept the 30-day notice as an account-specific exception (requires Risk sign-off).
2) Offer a compromise: 21-day notice + automatic notification + SCCs disclosure + commitment to consult for any new non-EEA subprocessors.

Procurement deadline is tight. If we can't get Risk sign-off by COB tomorrow, we should request a one-week extension from FinServCo.

-Monica
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-16T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA and subprocessor details needed to close purchase order

Monica — thanks for the summary. From a Risk & Compliance perspective:

- 30-day notice is operationally safe but increases our customer-facing obligations and could slow subprocessor rollouts. We can approve a customer-specific exception for a high-value deal if the account meets these controls: encryption at rest/in transit, SOC 2 Type II attestation on file, and annual subprocessor audits. FinServCo checks out on SOC 2 (they asked for evidence; I recommend sharing our SOC report and an attestation letter).
- Onward transfers: don't represent anything beyond SCCs in the DPA. Commit to not performing onward transfers except to subprocessors in our documented list; any deviation requires prior written consent.

If we take the exception route, I need a short risk memo (one pager) describing the justification, the compensating controls, and the owner for ongoing monitoring. Who will draft?

-Vivek
Head of Risk & Compliance
